Resolves #19070

The Workstation's toolbar gains **Start film tour**: the flagship film's screenplay (`apps/workstation/tour/fiveBeatFilm.mjs`) now carries runnable steps for all eight scenes and plays through the same `TourRunner` the dense tour uses. Its window beats ride surface cues over the existing `NativeGestureDriver` executors (tear-out with re-entry, committed tear-out, convert-while-dragging, whole-stack return), its perspective and history beats go through the workspace's own seams (`DockService#capturePerspective` / `#restorePerspective`, the Group cursor's undo and redo), and every vessel birth is preceded by a **gate** cue: playback holds until the viewer clicks **Continue**, which is the user activation `window.open` demands, so the window is born inside the viewer's gesture instead of being blocked as a popup. Replays and takes pass `autoGates: true`. The runner is untouched: a gate is a host cue held by the existing settlement boundary, not a new step type.

Evidence: L3 (real Chrome under Playwright with the live Neural Link bridge and the Brain runtime at `72fc142`: `WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs` 3/3 headless in 1.0 min and 3/3 headed — three vessels born through real Continue clicks in the viewer arm and without any click in the `autoGates` arm, retired, docked, returned, every window closed by the signature) → L3 required (AC-2, AC-3). Residual: AC-3's second engine (WebKit or Firefox) is not run by the e2e project, Residual-Owner: #15243 (the headed three-OS tear-out portability spike). Residual: AC-5 (a take recorded from the runnable script) is struck on the ticket and moves to the parent, Residual-Owner: #15252.

Micro-review eligible: no — one app file grows a cue vocabulary and a gate contract, and the screenplay's ordering encodes two measured driver preconditions.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here; the shared PR baseline runs.

Unit shape: `fiveBeatFilm.spec.mjs` › "every window birth is gated". |

## Deltas from ticket
- The runner stays document-tier: a gate is a host-side cue (accretion defence — the app already had the settlement seam the ticket wanted to add to the engine).
- Scene order: the morph (Metrics leaves and re-enters) now precedes the committed tear-out of the same pane, so tear-out → conversion → return stay contiguous as the five-beat witness proves them, and the film gains the "same pane, one more time: this time it stays" beat.
- Three measured driver preconditions shape the screenplay and are recorded as defect-notes: a tab folded into a tab bar's overflow menu is no drag handle (`did not arm` on Traces and on Audit as third tab of the narrow right group); a twelve-tab group re-enters without re-arming its reattach; and the stack return aims at the torn-out pane's stored home — my showcase had emptied that home, so the return fell back to the first tabs node (the 100k grid) and never settled in four runs. The showcase now docks Commits into that home group instead.
- The re-entry terminal reports `reentered: true` rather than `cancelled`; the controller accepts either as a legitimate un-applied settlement **only with the driver's `proof.documentsUnchanged === true`** — an un-applied terminal that cannot show the document byte-identical is a failure.
- **A failed cue fails its beat** (review round 1): the cue chain records the receipt and the error, and `settleTourStep` rejects on it, so the runner aborts before any later window effect runs on top of a world the screenplay no longer describes. The first draft resolved the failure to `false`, which let a failed morph be followed by the committed tear-out and the transfer.
- `autoGates` is a controller mode, not a per-run flag: `startTour({autoGates})` sets it when given and keeps it when omitted, so a transport can set the property before pressing the ordinary button (the e2e's unattended arm does exactly that through the fixture's `setProperties`).
- `perspective-capture` passes the perspective name as the record's `layoutId` — `capturePerspective` refuses without one.
- Two read-only oracles for whitebox specs: `getTourState()` (the bridge resolves property paths, not a method call mid-path) and `getCueLog()` (cue trail without proof documents, cue errors, vessel states, pending-ness probes) — the latter is what named each stalled beat.
- `cueVocabulary.mjs` (new, data-only) lets the screenplay's unit spec prove every cue it names is one the controller handles.

### `@neo-fable` commented on 2026-09-23T01:54:39Z

**CI unit red → fixed in c4d398893f.**

Root cause: `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs:490` plays `runVisibleTour` on a plain host object that only borrows the prototype's method — no `activeScript`, no instance helpers. The film rewrite had turned the static `TourController.totalBeats()` into an instance method reading `this.activeScript`, so that host threw `me.totalBeats is not a function`.

Fix: `totalBeats(script=workstationTourScript)` is static again and `runVisibleTour` counts the script it was handed. Local run: 147/147 workstation unit specs green, including `:490`. CI re-running.
